title: Organic Search Traffic Expansion to 500 Daily Clicks
description:
Audience: Self-taught developers, computer science students, and junior engineers in emerging tech markets seeking practical project tutorials.

Links: Google Search Central SEO Guide, Ahrefs Blog on Keyword Research

Tone: Direct, empirical, and technical.

Deadline: 48 hours (2 days solo).

Definition of "Done": Three targeted, low-competition long-tail technical articles are optimized, published, and indexed on zedu.chat, targeting specific developer pain points with integrated internal linking.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Give articles a real home and a crawl path first, then publish three cohort-learning tutorials
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Two things block 'published and indexed' today (checked 22 Oct 2026). First, zedu.chat has nowhere to publish an article: in the production code (Cybertron-HNG/zedu-fe, cybertron-integration) src/app/(homepage)/resources has only page.tsx and card components, no [slug] route, so each article needs a new resources/[slug] page with its own title, description and canonical. Second, robots.txt and sitemap.xml return the HTML page, so Google has no sitemap to find new URLs (a robots/sitemap task is open on another goal). Plan: 1) add the article route and confirm the sitemap fix includes it; 2) write three long-tail tutorials where the audience and Zedu genuinely meet, for example how self-taught developers run a study group or code-review circle in a cohort, each with real steps, code where relevant, and internal links to /products/channels and /products/buzz; 3) submit each URL for indexing in Search Console and record the indexed date. Tasks: article route and metadata (SEO), three tutorials (content), indexing check (SEO).

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Indexing proof, low-bandwidth format check, and a 48-hour clock that starts when an article can be crawled
acceptedWorkstreams.description:
Housekeeping first: an idea on this goal titled "Probe length limit" was mine, posted by accident while testing a field limit. Please reject it - it is withdrawn.

This idea owns the part neither accepted approach covers: proving the articles got indexed, and that they can be read on the connection the audience actually has.

Two facts shape it. (1) Sequencing: today zedu.chat has no article route - branch cybertron-integration has src/app/(homepage)/resources with only page.tsx and card components, no [slug] anywhere - and /sitemap.xml returns the app HTML, so a finished article cannot be indexed however well it is written. The 48-hour clock should start when the route and sitemap exist, or the "indexed" half of Done is unreachable through no fault of the writing. (2) Audience: self-taught developers and junior engineers on phones and metered data, so each article is checked for what that reader can use - readable with JavaScript disabled, a stated page-weight budget with no auto-playing media, copyable plain-text code blocks, and the answer to the query in the first screen.

Deliverables:
1) Indexing proof per article: live URL returning 200, present in the real sitemap, submitted in Search Console, then a dated re-check that it is actually indexed - each step a command with its output or a screenshot.
2) Format check per article with measurements: page weight, JS-off reading test, code-block copy test.
3) Internal-link spine: the three articles link in reading order and each links to one live Zedu page that answers the next question, target URLs shown.
4) A short note naming whatever blocked indexing (route, sitemap, Search Console), so delays are attributed correctly.

Peniel's cluster decides what to write; Irfat's route and sitemap work makes publishing possible. This one proves it worked.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Validate developer search demand and Zedu fit before choosing articles
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Before writing for a 500-click target, check real Search Console queries and a small sample of current search results for the proposed developer topics. Score each query for evidence of demand, realistic competition, and whether Zedu genuinely helps with the need. Map only the strongest queries to a suitable existing page or a clearly scoped tutorial, record the baseline and label uncertain volume. Deliver a short priority list and one article brief; do not publish or promise a traffic result.
